checks.name: original_send_suppressed

evidence.reason: Send snapshots the message and inserts it into controller.pending, then returns nil; there is no call to controller.wrapped.Send anywhere in the method.
The wrapped Transport is retained as a field, but no Send method dereferences it; the only Send implementation is the capturing wrapper.

checks.reason: MessageController.Send takes a deep snapshot, stores it in the pending map, and returns nil without ever invoking the wrapped transport, so a captured message cannot continue automatically along the original send path.

checks.name: protocol_logic_unchanged

evidence.reason: Patched Node.emit is identical to the original: it still iterates outbound messages and calls node.transport.Send; no protocol handler was changed.
Message.Clone and Entry.Clone are unchanged in the patched tree; the new controller depends on the existing deep-copy behavior.
MemoryTransport.Send is unchanged; the patch does not modify the original synchronous delivery path.

checks.reason: The patch adds only new files (message_controller.go and message_controller_test.go). The protocol core files node.go, message.go, and transport.go are byte-identical in the original and patched worktrees, so existing Tick/Step/Propose/emit logic and message cloning are unchanged.

checks.name: message_snapshot_stable

evidence.reason: Send assigns snapshot := message.Clone() before locking and stores that snapshot, isolating the pending store from the caller's original Message.
Clone allocates a new Entries slice and calls Entry.Clone for each entry, which deep-copies Entry.Data via append([]byte(nil), ...).
ListPending calls captured.copy(), which re-clones the Message field before returning, so returned CapturedMessage values do not share slice state with the store.

checks.reason: Capture clones the message before storing it, Entry.Data is deep-copied, and ListPending returns another deep copy, so later mutation of the caller's message or of the returned metadata cannot corrupt the pending store.

checks.name: exact_target_preserved

evidence.reason: Send stores To: snapshot.To in the CapturedMessage metadata.
Inject resolves target := controller.nodes[captured.To], using the recorded target rather than any caller-supplied target.
Inject delivers captured.Message.Clone(), whose To remains snapshot.To, so the delivered Message matches the recorded target.
Node.Step rejects delivery when message.To != node.id, guaranteeing injection enters the exact recorded target's normal protocol input boundary.

checks.reason: The controller records the message's To at capture time, resolves the injection target from that recorded To, and delivers a clone whose To field is unchanged. Node.Step enforces that the message is delivered only to the recorded target node.

checks.name: failed_injection_preserves_pending

evidence.reason: If target.Step returns an error, Inject returns the wrapped error immediately and never executes the delete.
delete(controller.pending, id) is executed only after target.Step returns nil.

checks.reason: In the sequential case, Inject returns on target.Step error before reaching the delete, and the delete happens only after a successful Step, so a failed delivery leaves the selected pending message in the store.

checks.name: existing_tests_unchanged

evidence.reason: The patched node_test.go matches the original file exactly; existing tests and helpers such as newThreeNodeCluster and electNode are unchanged.
New controller tests are additive in a new file and do not modify the existing node_test.go suite.

checks.reason: No existing test file was modified. The original and patched node_test.go are identical, and the new controller tests are contained in a separate new file, so existing test behavior is not edited or weakened.

checks.name: testing_contract_conformance

evidence.reason: Inject performs the pending lookup under controller.mu, but unlocks at line 134 before calling target.Step and only re-locks at line 140 to delete; the delivery portion is therefore not serialized.
ClearPending can acquire controller.mu and replace the pending map while an Inject is still inside target.Step, because Inject holds no controller lock during delivery.
The single sync.Mutex guards the pending map but is not held for the entire Inject operation, so it does not provide the required operation-level serialization.

checks.reason: The required API shape is present (NewMessageController(Transport), ListPending, ClearPending, Inject), capture is active immediately after construction with no weakening toggle, and the message_id_scope is declared. However, the public contract requires Inject and ClearPending to be serialized. Inject releases controller.mu before target.Step and reacquires it only for the final delete, so two concurrent Inject calls for the same MessageID can both pass the lookup and deliver the same pending message, and ClearPending can interleave with an in-progress delivery. This violates serialization of test-controller operations and the guarantee that a successful injection consumes exactly the selected pending message.

issues.reason: Inject releases the controller mutex during target.Step. Concurrent Inject calls for the same MessageID can both read the pending record and deliver the same message twice, and ClearPending can run during delivery. This breaks the required serialization of Inject/ClearPending and the exactly-once consumption guarantee for successful injection.

risks: Inject requires target nodes to be registered separately via Register; if a captured message's To node is not registered, Inject returns ErrUnknownTargetNode and leaves the message pending. This is an extra API not specified in the public testing contract, though it does not weaken the promised capture behavior.
The wrapped Transport is retained but never invoked, which is correct for v0.1 test-mode suppression, but the implementation has no production mode path.
The concurrency issue is not caught by the added concurrent test because that test only exercises Send/ListPending/ClearPending and does not run Inject concurrently with Inject or ClearPending.
